federal.rule: CDC rules depend on where the dog was vaccinated and which countries it was in during the past 6 months. Every dog needs the free CDC Dog Import Form receipt, must look healthy, be at least 6 months old and have a microchip readable by a universal scanner.

federal.topic: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries
federal.rule: Only the CDC Dog Import Form receipt is needed (valid 6 months for multiple entries unless the dog visits a high-risk or different country). Any airport, seaport or land port.

federal.topic: US-vaccinated dogs returning from high-risk countries
federal.rule: CDC Dog Import Form receipt plus the Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination form, completed by a USDA-accredited vet and endorsed by USDA before the dog leaves the US. Microchip before the rabies vaccine; first vaccine at 12 weeks or older and at least 28 days before. USDA export certificates issued after July 31, 2025 are not accepted instead.

Certification of Foreign Rabies Vaccination and Microchip form (government-vet endorsed, within 30 days of travel), a valid rabies titer from a CDC-approved lab, and a reservation at a CDC-registered animal care facility (28-day quarantine if no valid titer). Must arrive by air at that facility's airport.

federal.topic: Dogs from screwworm or FMD-affected countries (USDA)
federal.rule: Screwworm: certificate from an official vet that the dog was inspected within 5 days before shipment. FMD: bathe the dog and keep it away from livestock for 5 days (no documents).

CDC: cats must appear healthy and may be inspected; no proof of rabies vaccination required (recommended). USDA APHIS has no animal health requirements for pet cats. State and airline rules still apply; Hawaii and Guam quarantine rules apply to all cats.
The destination country sets the rules. A USDA-accredited vet prepares the health certificate and submits it to APHIS for endorsement through VEHCS.
APHIS does not regulate pet owners moving pets between states; the receiving state or territory sets the requirements.
USDA: airlines may require a health and acclimation certificate signed by a licensed vet within 10 days of travel; some states and countries require a rabies certificate.

train.heading: By train (Amtrak)
rules: Dogs and cats only, at least 8 weeks old with vaccinations current; one pet per passenger and one pet per carrier.
20 lb max, pet plus carrier combined. Leak-proof, ventilated carrier, max 19 x 14 x 10.5 in, under your own seat; it counts as a carry-on.
Up to 7 hours, including connections. Coach and Acela Business only (not First Class, sleeping cars or food service cars; not the Quiet Car on Keystone and Pennsylvanian).
Reserve a spot for your pet; the fee varies by route. Sign the Pet Release online and check in 45 minutes before departure at staffed stations.
Auto Train, Gold Runner and Amtrak Connection services, or to Canada on the Adirondack, Maple Leaf and Amtrak Cascades.
train.service_animals_note: Service animals are accepted on all trains.

territories.name: Guam
territories.rule: Entry permit, current and prior rabies certificates, microchip, OIE-FAVN test from a CDC-approved lab, quarantine reservation and a health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet within 10 days of travel. Submit documents 30+ days ahead; $65 fee. Pets from the US can do up to 5 days in commercial quarantine, then finish the 120-day period at home.

territories.name: US Virgin Islands
territories.rule: From the US or Puerto Rico: health certificate (APHIS 7001, official state CVI or approved eCVI) within 10 days of arrival, emailed at least 1 business day before. Current rabies vaccination (or adequate FAVN titer within 12 months); 10 days must pass after a first rabies vaccine.

territories.name: Puerto Rico
territories.rule: See the state table: health certificate valid 30 days, rabies within 6 months for pets over 4 months, parasite treatment within 72 hours.

states.name: Alabama
states.rabies: Required at 3 months or older (under 3 months exempt)
states.notes: APHIS Form 7001 not accepted as a CVI since 2019. Exhibition stays under 21 days are exempt.

states.name: Alaska
states.rabies: Check with state veterinarian
states.notes: We could not load the official Alaska page this session (bot check). Confirm with the Alaska Office of the State Veterinarian.

states.name: Arizona
states.rabies: Current vaccination at 12 weeks or older, listed on the CVI
states.notes: Rabies titers are not accepted instead of vaccination. No entry permit needed. Airlines may have their own CVI rules.

states.name: Arkansas
states.rabies: Within 12 months before entry; dogs and cats under 4 months exempt
states.notes: A 3-year vaccine is accepted if the pet had at least one previous rabies vaccine (2 CAR § 195-207).

states.name: California
states.cvi: No, for pets not changing ownership
states.rabies: Not set by CDFA (rabies questions go to the CA Dept. of Public Health)
states.notes: CDFA has no entry requirements for pet dogs and cats that are not changing ownership. Since Jan 1, 2025, dogs entering to be sold or adopted need a CVI issued within 10 days and submitted to CDFA.

states.name: Colorado
states.rabies: Check with state veterinarian
states.notes: Confirmed: dogs and cats from states with an active New World screwworm infested zone need a CVI issued within 5 days before entry (emergency rule of June 10, 2026). The general pet page could not be loaded this session.

states.name: Connecticut
states.rabies: Proof of current vaccination for dogs and cats over 3 months
states.notes: Pets must not come from a rabies quarantine area or have been exposed to rabies in the past 100 days.

states.name: Delaware
states.rabies: Dogs over 4 months; cats 6 months or older
states.notes: Dogs' rabies vaccine type and date must be on the health certificate (3 DE Admin. Code 904).

states.name: District of Columbia
states.cvi: Yes, issued within 30 days of travel
states.rabies: Dogs (rabies and distemper) and cats (rabies) vaccinated at least 30 days before travel
states.notes: The 30-day gap between vaccination and travel is stricter than most states.

states.name: Florida
states.cvi: Not for privately owned pets traveling with their owner; otherwise CVI within 30 days
states.rabies: Required at 3 months or older
states.notes: Pets from New World screwworm infested zones need a Certificate of Animal Movement with a permission number. FDACS notes most airlines want a health certificate within 7-10 days of travel.

states.name: Georgia
states.cvi: Not for pets traveling with their owner; CVI within 30 days for pets for sale
states.rabies: Proof required for dogs and cats 12 weeks or older
states.notes: A rabies vaccination record is sufficient for pets traveling with their owners.

states.name: Hawaii
states.cvi: Yes, plus a full rabies quarantine program
states.rabies: Two rabies vaccinations plus a passing OIE-FAVN test to avoid quarantine
states.notes: Rabies-free state. All dogs and cats of any age must meet HAR 4-29. The 5 Day Or Less program allows direct airport release in Honolulu; pets that do not qualify face up to 120 days of quarantine. Wait at least 30 days after a passing FAVN and 30 days after the most recent rabies shot. Send documents 10+ days before arrival or the fee rises ($185 to $244 per pet for direct release).

states.name: Idaho
states.rabies: Current vaccination at 12 weeks or older (1- or 3-year vaccine)
states.notes: APHIS Form 7001 not accepted. From New World screwworm affected states, the CVI must be issued within 5 days of movement.

states.name: Illinois
states.rabies: Required at 16 weeks or older, recorded on the CVI

states.name: Indiana
states.rabies: Required at 3 months or older
states.notes: APHIS 7001 accepted only in a USDA-validated form. Pets from New World screwworm zones need a movement certificate, CVI and treatment within 5 days (from June 9, 2026).

states.name: Iowa
states.rabies: Dogs 4 months or older; no rabies vaccination required for cats
states.notes: Pets from rabies-quarantined areas are not admitted. Dogs for exhibition entering for a limited time are exempt from the CVI (IAC 21-65.10).

states.name: Kansas
states.rabies: Proof of current vaccination for dogs and cats over 3 months
states.notes: APHIS Form 7001 not accepted. Pets from New World screwworm infested zones need a permit and an NWS-free statement on the CVI.

states.name: Kentucky
states.cvi: Yes, for any purpose (service dogs exempt)
states.rabies: Over 4 months, per the NASPHV Compendium
states.notes: Service dogs need a current rabies certificate instead of a CVI (302 KAR 20:040).

states.name: Louisiana
states.rabies: Check with state veterinarian
states.notes: We could not find Louisiana's dog and cat rule on an official state page this session. Confirm with the Louisiana Department of Agriculture and Forestry.

states.name: Maine
states.rabies: Check with state veterinarian
states.notes: Only Maine's rescue/adoption import rules (shelter import permit, rabies at 3 months or older) could be confirmed this session; confirm pet-owner travel rules with Maine DACF Animal Health.

states.name: Maryland
states.rabies: At least one rabies vaccination (pets under 4 months exempt), stated on the CVI
states.notes: CVI must state the pet is not from a rabies quarantine area and not exposed in the past 6 months. Dogs entering temporarily for exhibition are exempt. Source document dated 2018.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.rabies: Within 12 months before entry if over 6 months; unvaccinated pets must be vaccinated within 30 days of entry or at 6 months
states.notes: The health certificate must show non-exposure to rabies.

states.name: Michigan
states.cvi: Yes, from a USDA-accredited vet (dogs and cats)
states.rabies: Dogs 12 weeks or older; for cats, rabies is stated only for shelter and pet-shop imports
states.notes: Separate rules apply to dogs and cats for shelters, pet shops and exhibition. New screwworm import requirements apply.

states.name: Minnesota
states.cvi: Only if moving in, staying over 30 days, or changing owner
states.rabies: Required at 3 months or older
states.notes: Temporary visits under 30 days with no change of owner need no CVI. From July 1, 2026 all CVIs must be electronic. Pets from NWS-infested states: CVI within 72 hours, treatment, and a 5-day quarantine.

states.name: Mississippi
states.cvi: Not for pets accompanied by their owner
states.rabies: Proof required at 3 months or older
states.notes: CVI needed for exhibition, change of ownership, adoption, or pets traveling without their owner.

states.name: Missouri
states.rabies: Check with state veterinarian
states.notes: Only Missouri's exhibition rules could be confirmed this session (CVI required, rabies at 4 months or older). Confirm general pet travel rules with the Missouri Department of Agriculture.

states.name: Montana
states.cvi: Not for pets traveling with their owner
states.rabies: Proof of current vaccination required (certificate should travel with the pet)
states.notes: Health certificate within 30 days for change of ownership or shelter/rescue transfers.

states.name: Nebraska
states.rabies: CVI must certify current rabies vaccination
states.notes: Unvaccinated dogs and cats over 3 months must be vaccinated within 30 days after arrival.

states.name: Nevada
states.rabies: Current, per the NASPHV Compendium
states.notes: No permit required.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.rabies: Required at 3 months or older; younger pets within 30 days of turning 3 months
states.notes: Pets must not come from a rabies-quarantined area (Agr 2112).

states.name: New Jersey
states.cvi: Dogs: yes, within 30 days. Cats: no specific requirement
states.rabies: Not specifically required for import; dogs 7 months or older must be licensed (rabies vaccine needed for a license)
states.notes: Source document dated August 2017.

states.name: New Mexico
states.rabies: Check with state veterinarian
states.notes: We could not find New Mexico's dog and cat entry rule on an official page this session. Confirm with the New Mexico Livestock Board.

states.name: New York
states.cvi: Yes, within 30 days, unless staying under 30 days
states.rabies: Required at 3 months or older (1- or 3-year vaccine)
states.notes: NY residents' licensed dogs returning within a year are exempt. New York City has extra rules.

states.name: North Carolina
states.cvi: State public health says it is eliminating the CVI requirement for dogs, cats and ferrets
states.rabies: Unvaccinated pets 4 months or older must be vaccinated within 1 week of entry
states.notes: The official page wording is in transition; confirm the current CVI rule before travel.

states.name: North Dakota
states.rabies: Required over 12 weeks; a copy of the certificate must accompany the pet
states.notes: APHIS Form 7001 not accepted. Pets from NWS states need a pre-entry permit.

states.name: Ohio
states.rabies: Required at 12 weeks or older, with a NASPHV Form 51 rabies certificate
states.notes: Ohio Adm. Code 901:1-17-05 (version effective Sept 11, 2026).

states.name: Oklahoma
states.rabies: Within 12 months before entry at 3 months (12 weeks) or older
states.notes: A 3-year vaccine is recognized if primary and booster doses are on the CVI.

states.name: Oregon
states.cvi: Yes, issued within 30 days (official serial-numbered CVI)
states.rabies: Per the NASPHV Compendium, listed on the CVI

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.rabies: Check with state veterinarian
states.notes: Confirmed: no import permit for dogs or cats, and APHIS Form 7001 is not accepted. The official page does not state the pet dog and cat CVI rule.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.rabies: Required at 3 months or older; adults 6+ months with only a first vaccine must wait 30 days
states.notes: Puppies and kittens 3-6 months with a first vaccine may enter immediately (250-RICR-40-05-1).

states.name: South Carolina
states.rabies: Proof of vaccination required
states.notes: Pets must not come from a rabies quarantine area.

states.name: South Dakota
states.cvi: Not if traveling with owner and staying under 30 days
states.rabies: Proof required at 3 months or older
states.notes: Pets under rabies quarantine or showing disease may not enter.

states.name: Tennessee
states.cvi: Only if staying more than 15 days (valid 30 days)
states.rabies: Dogs 3 months or older; cats 6 months or older
states.notes: Call the state office for imports from Texas (screwworm).

states.name: Texas
states.rabies: Required at 12 weeks or older, with a rabies certificate
states.notes: If the first vaccine was given within the last 30 days, keep the pet confined for the rest of those 30 days.

states.name: Utah
states.cvi: Only in special cases (pets under treatment for a transmissible disease, from abroad, or from NWS-infested states)
states.rabies: Current vaccination if over 12 weeks
states.notes: Puppies and kittens under 8 weeks must travel with their mother.

states.name: Vermont
states.cvi: Not for relocation, vacation or school; yes for sale, exchange or adoption
states.rabies: Over 3 months, stated on the certificate for pets imported for sale or adoption
states.notes: Pets from NWS states must be treated and have a CVI within 5 days of entry.

states.name: Virginia
states.cvi: Not for personally owned pets; CVI within 10 days for sale, adoption, breeding or promotion
states.rabies: No state entry requirement for personally owned pets
states.notes: No permit required.

states.name: Washington
states.cvi: Not for family pets traveling with their owner with a current rabies certificate; otherwise yes
states.rabies: Current vaccination; pets under 90 days exempt
states.notes: Dogs 6 months or older need a negative heartworm test or preventive unless owned over a month and traveling with the owner (WAC 16-54-170).

states.name: West Virginia
states.rabies: Within the previous 12 months for dogs and cats over 6 months

states.name: Wisconsin
states.cvi: Yes, by any mode of transport
states.rabies: Dogs and cats 5 months or older, with date and due date on the CVI
states.notes: Computer-generated APHIS 7001 not accepted. Heartworm-positive dogs must finish treatment first.

states.name: Wyoming
states.cvi: Not for pets traveling with owner (no change of ownership)
states.rabies: Proof of current vaccination at 3 months (12 weeks) or older
states.notes: CVI within 30 days for sale, adoption, shelter or rescue; breeding dogs need a Brucella canis test.

states.name: Puerto Rico
states.cvi: Yes, official health certificate valid 30 days
states.rabies: Dogs and cats over 4 months vaccinated within the 6 months before shipment
states.notes: External parasite treatment within 72 hours before entry and ID (microchip or collar tag) required. No import permit for interstate moves.
